Source format: Protocol and site master file

The site is led by the Principal Investigator (PI) for each protocol, with
support from a Site Coordinator, Clinical Research Associates (CRAs), and
administrative staff. The delegation of duties is recorded in the Site Delegation
Log, which is maintained in the DMS and reviewed at each study initiation.

3. Current Protocol Listing

The following table lists the active protocols currently managed by Meridian
Clinical Research. The protocol summaries are maintained in the DMS and are
version-controlled. Any amendment to a protocol summary is reviewed by the PI and
QA before the updated version is uploaded.

| Protocol Number | Title | Sponsor | Principal Investigator |
|-----------------|-------|---------|------------------------|
| THX-2024-01 | A Phase 2, Randomised, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study of THX-2024 in Patients with Moderate-to-Severe Atopic Dermatitis | Thalex Biopharmaceuticals | Dr. Marcus Tan |

Note: The protocol summary for THX-2024-01 is listed as current in the DMS as of
the date of this SMF. The summary includes the study design, inclusion/exclusion
criteria, and the schedule of assessments. Any updates to the protocol summary
will be reflected in the DMS with a new version number and a revision date.

4. Document Management System

The Meridian DMS is the central repository for all trial-related documents,
including protocol summaries, informed consent forms, case report forms, and
correspondence with sponsors and regulatory authorities. The DMS is accessed via
a secure internal portal, and access is restricted to authorised personnel.

Documents in the DMS follow a standard naming convention, for example,
"Brochure_Protocol_THX-2024-01_v1.2". Each document is assigned a unique document
ID and is time-stamped with the date and time of upload. The system maintains a
full revision history, allowing users to view previous versions and track changes.

The QA unit performs a quarterly audit of the DMS to ensure that all documents are
current and that no obsolete versions remain accessible. Any discrepancies found
during the audit are documented and corrected within five working days.

5. Current Protocol Summary Details

The Meridian Clinical Research protocol summary lists has_trial_protocol THX-2024-01. Record status: current.

The summary for THX-2024-01 is maintained in the DMS under the document ID
"THX-2024-01_Summary_v1.3". It was last reviewed and approved by Dr. Marcus Tan on
5 July 2026. The summary is considered current and in effect for the duration of
the trial.

6. Site Identification

Meridian Clinical Research is identified in the DMS and in all correspondence with
the sponsor as Site Number 01 for protocol THX-2024-01. The site is registered with
the HSA under the Clinical Trial Certificate number CTC-2024-0187.

7. Document Control Procedures

All documents uploaded to the DMS must be approved by the relevant study team
member before they are made accessible to other users. The approval process is
recorded in the DMS, including the approver's name and the date of approval.
Documents that are no longer current are archived and marked as "Superseded" in
the DMS. Archived documents are retained for a minimum of 10 years as per
regulatory requirements.

Any staff member who identifies a document error or discrepancy is required to
notify the QA unit immediately. The QA unit will then initiate a document
correction, which includes a review of the error, an update to the document, and
the issuance of a new version number.

8. Contact Information

For queries regarding this Site Master File or the DMS, please contact:

Quality Assurance Unit
Meridian Clinical Research
15 Tampines Industrial Avenue 5
Singapore 528761
Email: qa@meridiancr.sg
Phone: +65 6789 1234
- Administrator: full system control, including user account management, role assignment,
  audit log export, and system configuration. Administrator access is restricted to two
  named staff in the IT department and one staff member in the QA unit. No other personnel
  are granted Administrator rights, and any change to the Administrator list must be
  documented in the DMS audit trail and reported to the sponsor within five working days.

Access to the DMS is limited to the site network or through the approved VPN connection.
Remote access requires the user's account to be flagged as "Remote Capable" by the IT
department, and all remote sessions are logged with the user's IP address and session
duration.

The DMS also maintains a user access log that records the following for each login:

- User ID
- Date and time of login and logout
- IP address or workstation identifier
- Documents opened, viewed, or downloaded during the session

These logs are retained for a minimum of five years and are reviewed by the QA unit on a
quarterly basis to identify any unusual access patterns, such as repeated failed login
attempts or access to documents outside a user's role scope.

10. Versioning and Document Naming Conventions

All controlled documents stored in the DMS follow a standard naming convention to ensure
consistency and ease of retrieval. The convention is:

[Document Type]_[Protocol Number]_[Description]_v[Major].[Minor]

For example, the current protocol summary is stored as "Brochure_Protocol_THX-2024-01_v1.3",
where "Brochure_Protocol" indicates the document type, "THX-2024-01" is the protocol number,
and "v1.3" is the version number.

The site master file describes Document Management System system_name Document Management System. Record status: current.

The version number consists of a major and a minor component. A minor version increment
(e.g., v1.1 to v1.2) is used for editorial corrections, formatting changes, or clarifications
that do not alter the scientific or regulatory content of the document. A major version
increment (e.g., v1.3 to v2.0) is used when the content is substantially revised, such as a
change to the study design, endpoints, or safety information.

When a document is uploaded for the first time, it is assigned version v0.1 and is considered
a draft. Draft documents are visible only to the Contributor who uploaded them and to any
Reviewers or Approvers designated by the QA unit. Once the document is approved, it becomes
v1.0 and is made visible to all users.

Each time a document is revised, the DMS automatically creates a new version while preserving
the previous version in the system's revision history. The previous version is marked as
"Superseded" and remains accessible only to users with Reviewer privileges or higher.
Superseded versions cannot be edited or deleted, and they are retained for the full
regulatory retention period of 10 years.

The DMS also records a revision history for each document that includes:

- Version number
- Date and time of upload
- Author (the user who uploaded the version)
- Summary of changes (entered by the author at the time of upload)
- Approval status and approver details

This revision history is viewable by any user with access to the document, and it forms the
basis of the audit trail required by the sponsor and by the Health Sciences Authority (HSA).

11. Audit Trail and Compliance

The DMS maintains an audit trail that captures all significant actions performed on
controlled documents. The audit trail is write-once, meaning that entries cannot be edited,
deleted, or overwritten by any user, including Administrators. Each audit entry records:

- Date and time stamp (in Singapore Standard Time, UTC+8)
- User ID of the person performing the action
- Action type (e.g., upload, edit, approve, archive, supersede, download)
- Document ID and version number affected
- A description of the action, where applicable
12. Distribution of Controlled Documents

The QA unit is responsible for the distribution of all controlled documents. Distribution is performed exclusively through the DMS, using the "Distribution" function, which generates a notification to the designated recipients and records the date and time of distribution in the audit trail. Hard copies of controlled documents are not permitted for use at the site, except where a hard copy is required by a regulatory authority during an inspection, or where a device or system at the site is not connected to the DMS. In such cases, the hard copy must be stamped "CONTROLLED COPY" and assigned to a named individual. The named individual is responsible for returning the hard copy to the QA unit when it is superseded, or for destroying it in the presence of a QA witness. The QA unit maintains a log of all hard copies issued, which includes the document ID and version, the recipient's name, the date of issue, and the date of return or destruction.

13. Document Review and Approval

Each controlled document is subject to a defined review and approval process before it is released for use. The process is initiated by the Document Owner, who is the person with primary responsibility for the content of the document. The Document Owner is typically the Principal Investigator for protocol-related documents, the Medical Writer for the protocol and the informed consent form, or the relevant department head for standard operating procedures and work instructions.

The Document Owner uploads the draft document to the DMS and designates a set of Reviewers. Reviewers are selected based on their expertise and their role in the conduct of the trial. For example, the protocol is reviewed by the Principal Investigator, the Clinical Research Coordinator, the Data Manager, and the site's Biostatistician, where applicable. The Regulatory Affairs Officer reviews all documents that are submitted to the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) or to the institutional review board (IRB), to confirm that the documents are complete and consistent with the current regulations and the approved submission.

Reviewers have 10 working days to complete their review. The DMS sends a reminder to any Reviewer who has not submitted comments after 7 working days. If a Reviewer does not submit comments within the 10-working-day period, the Document Owner may either extend the review period or proceed with the approval, provided that the Reviewer has confirmed in writing (which may be by email) that they have no comments. This confirmation is recorded in the DMS as part of the revision history.

Once all Reviewer comments have been addressed and the document has been updated, the Document Owner submits the document for approval. The Approver is a person with the authority to approve the document for use. For the protocol and the informed consent form, the Approver is the Principal Investigator. For site-level standard operating procedures, the Approver is the Director of Clinical Operations. For documents that relate to the conduct of the trial at the site, the Approver is the Sponsor's Medical Monitor, where the sponsor has reserved this authority in the clinical trial agreement.

The Approver receives a notification from the DMS and has 5 working days to review the final version of the document. If the Approver does not act within this period, the DMS escalates the matter to the QA unit, who contacts the Approver directly. The approval is recorded in the DMS with the Approver's user ID, the date and time of approval, and a statement that the Approver has reviewed the document and approves it for use. Once approved, the document is assigned version v1.0 (or a higher major version, if the document has been previously approved) and is made visible to all users.

Access to the DMS is limited to the site network or through the approved VPN connection.
Remote access requires the user's account to be flagged as "Remote Capable" by the IT
department, and all remote sessions are logged with the user's IP address and session
duration.

The DMS also maintains a user access log that records the following for each login:

- User ID
- Date and time of login and logout
- IP address or workstation identifier
- Documents opened, viewed, or downloaded during the session

These logs are retained for a minimum of five years and are reviewed by the QA unit on a
quarterly basis to identify any unusual access patterns, such as repeated failed login
attempts or access to documents outside a user's role scope.

10. Versioning and Document Naming Conventions

All controlled documents stored in the DMS follow a standard naming convention to ensure
consistency and ease of retrieval. The convention is:

[Document Type]_[Protocol Number]_[Description]_v[Major].[Minor]

For example, the current protocol summary is stored as "Brochure_Protocol_THX-2024-01_v1.3",
where "Brochure_Protocol" indicates the document type, "THX-2024-01" is the protocol number,
and "v1.3" is the version number.

The site master file describes Document Management System system_name Document Management System. Record status: current.

The version number consists of a major and a minor component. A minor version increment
(e.g., v1.1 to v1.2) is used for editorial corrections, formatting changes, or clarifications
that do not alter the scientific or regulatory content of the document. A major version
increment (e.g., v1.3 to v2.0) is used when the content is substantially revised, such as a
change to the study design, endpoints, or safety information.

When a document is uploaded for the first time, it is assigned version v0.1 and is considered
a draft. Draft documents are visible only to the Contributor who uploaded them and to any
Reviewers or Approvers designated by the QA unit. Once the document is approved, it becomes
v1.0 and is made visible to all users.

Each time a document is revised, the DMS automatically creates a new version while preserving
the previous version in the system's revision history. The previous version is marked as
"Superseded" and remains accessible only to users with Reviewer privileges or higher.
Superseded versions cannot be edited or deleted, and they are retained for the full
regulatory retention period of 10 years.

The DMS also records a revision history for each document that includes:

- Version number
- Date and time of upload
- Author (the user who uploaded the version)
- Summary of changes (entered by the author at the time of upload)
- Approval status and approver details

This revision history is viewable by any user with access to the document, and it forms the
basis of the audit trail required by the sponsor and by the Health Sciences Authority (HSA).

11. Audit Trail and Compliance

The DMS maintains an audit trail that captures all significant actions performed on
controlled documents. The audit trail is write-once, meaning that entries cannot be edited,
deleted, or overwritten by any user, including Administrators. Each audit entry records:

- Date and time stamp (in Singapore Standard Time, UTC+8)
- User ID of the person performing the action
- Action type (e.g., upload, edit, approve, archive, supersede, download)
- Document ID and version number affected
- A description of the action, where applicable

12. Distribution of Controlled Documents

The QA unit is responsible for the distribution of all controlled documents. Distribution is performed exclusively through the DMS, using the "Distribution" function, which generates a notification to the designated recipients and records the date and time of distribution in the audit trail. Hard copies of controlled documents are not permitted for use at the site, except where a hard copy is required by a regulatory authority during an inspection, or where a device or system at the site is not connected to the DMS. In such cases, the hard copy must be stamped "CONTROLLED COPY" and assigned to a named individual. The named individual is responsible for returning the hard copy to the QA unit when it is superseded, or for destroying it in the presence of a QA witness. The QA unit maintains a log of all hard copies issued, which includes the document ID and version, the recipient's name, the date of issue, and the date of return or destruction.

13. Document Review and Approval

Each controlled document is subject to a defined review and approval process before it is released for use. The process is initiated by the Document Owner, who is the person with primary responsibility for the content of the document. The Document Owner is typically the Principal Investigator for protocol-related documents, the Medical Writer for the protocol and the informed consent form, or the relevant department head for standard operating procedures and work instructions.

The Document Owner uploads the draft document to the DMS and designates a set of Reviewers. Reviewers are selected based on their expertise and their role in the conduct of the trial. For example, the protocol is reviewed by the Principal Investigator, the Clinical Research Coordinator, the Data Manager, and the site's Biostatistician, where applicable. The Regulatory Affairs Officer reviews all documents that are submitted to the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) or to the institutional review board (IRB), to confirm that the documents are complete and consistent with the current regulations and the approved submission.

Reviewers have 10 working days to complete their review. The DMS sends a reminder to any Reviewer who has not submitted comments after 7 working days. If a Reviewer does not submit comments within the 10-working-day period, the Document Owner may either extend the review period or proceed with the approval, provided that the Reviewer has confirmed in writing (which may be by email) that they have no comments. This confirmation is recorded in the DMS as part of the revision history.

Once all Reviewer comments have been addressed and the document has been updated, the Document Owner submits the document for approval. The Approver is a person with the authority to approve the document for use. For the protocol and the informed consent form, the Approver is the Principal Investigator. For site-level standard operating procedures, the Approver is the Director of Clinical Operations. For documents that relate to the conduct of the trial at the site, the Approver is the Sponsor's Medical Monitor, where the sponsor has reserved this authority in the clinical trial agreement.

The Approver receives a notification from the DMS and has 5 working days to review the final version of the document. If the Approver does not act within this period, the DMS escalates the matter to the QA unit, who contacts the Approver directly. **Effective Date**

The Safety Language Update shall take effect on **15 September 2024**. All sites are required to implement the updated documents for any subject who provides consent on or after this date. Subjects who have already provided consent using the previous version of the documents are not required to re-consent solely on the basis of this update, unless otherwise determined by the site's Institutional Review Board (IRB) or the sponsor's medical monitor.

Please note that the effective date of 15 September 2024 is the date on which the updated documents become the only valid version for new consent. This date has been set to allow sufficient time for translation, site-level review, and IRB approval of the amended documents where required.

**Description of Required Changes**

The following changes are to be made to the patient information brochure (Version 3.0, dated 12 June 2024) and the corresponding informed consent form (Version 3.0, dated 12 June 2024):

1.  **Adverse Event Reporting**: A new subsection titled "Reporting of Side Effects" is to be added to Section 6 (Risks and Discomforts) of the brochure. This subsection must clearly state that subjects, or their legally acceptable representative, may report any suspected side effect directly to the study site staff, or to the sponsor's safety hotline at +65 6222 4199 (available 24 hours). The subsection must also include the following sentence: "You may also report side effects to the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) through the HSA Adverse Event Reporting System at www.hsa.gov.sg/report-adverse-event."

2.  **Contact Details**: The contact details for the Principal Investigator and the study coordinator are to be updated to reflect the current personnel. Please replace the existing contact information with the following:

*   Principal Investigator: Dr. Lim Wei Sheng, Department of Neurology, Singapore General Hospital. Telephone: +65 6321 4321. Email: wei.sheng.lim@singhealth.com.sg
    *   Study Coordinator: Ms. Nurul Aini Binte Abdul Rahman, Clinical Research Coordinator. Telephone: +65 6321 4890. Email: nurul.aini@singhealth.com.sg

Regulatory correspondence states Safety Language Update effective_date 2024-09-15. Record status: current.

3.  **Compensation for Injury**: A clarification is to be added to Section 9 (Compensation for Injury) stating that compensation for research-related injury will be provided in accordance with the sponsor's insurance policy, and that a copy of the policy summary is available upon request from the study site.

4.  **Updated Version Numbering**: The updated documents are to be designated as Version 4.0, dated 15 September 2024. The document control number on the footer of each page must be updated accordingly.

**Submission Requirements**

Please submit the following to the Regulatory Affairs department no later than **30 August 2024**:

*   A tracked-changes version of the updated patient information brochure and informed consent form.
*   A clean version of each document.
*   A summary of changes table (document title, version, date, and a brief description of each change).

The updated documents must be submitted to the respective IRB for approval prior to implementation. For sites where the IRB requires a formal amendment submission, please ensure that the amendment is submitted with reference to this letter and the HSA correspondence cited above.

**Current Status**

Please be informed that the Safety Language Update is the current and active requirement for this study. The previous version of the patient information brochure (Version 3.0) remains valid for consenting activities until 14 September 2024. After this date, only the updated documents (Version 4.0) may be used for new consent.
